title: Examples, boundary tests and properties

objectives.text: Write tests for normal inputs, boundary values and declared errors.
State and check an invariant while recognising that tested cases are not a universal proof.

blocks.markdown: A passing test establishes a result for the case it actually executed. It is not a proof for every possible input or proof that the specification is right. Start with an explicit contract: this fee function accepts exact nonnegative integers and returns their product in cents, raising ValueError otherwise. Test both accepted values and rejected inputs.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 2, then True. The subcases include boundary/type errors; testsRun counts the two test methods, not every assertion.

blocks.markdown: A test needs an independent reason to expect its result. Copying the implementation expression into a test can repeat the same mistake. For a small example, compute the result by hand. For another check, compare with an independently structured implementation or a mathematical identity. Agree the rounding/domain rules before choosing the oracle.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 144. This exhaustively checks a small finite domain, not all nonnegative integers.

blocks.markdown: The property fee(a+b,r)=fee(a,r)+fee(b,r) follows from exact multiplication with the stated domain. A tiered fee or per-trade rounding policy might not satisfy it. A property that contradicts the real contract is a bad test. Include a deliberately broken implementation, such as (qty+1)*rate, to check that your examples can actually fail. A test suite that never fails even for an obvious bug is not providing useful evidence.

Do not rely on bare assert for production input validation: Python can disable those assertions in optimised execution. The worked property check uses an explicit conditional and raises AssertionError. unittest assertions are methods and are not the same as a bare assert statement.

Independent transfer: test a total_quantities function that rejects an entire list if any element is not an exact nonnegative integer. Include empty input, one valid value, zero, a negative, bool and text. Then intentionally change the implementation to accept bool and confirm that the relevant test fails. Restore the implementation after observing the failure. All work can run locally with the supplied synthetic cases.

Technical references: [Python unittest reference](https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html) for test methods, expected errors and assertion methods. The financial schemas, policies and synthetic cases in this lesson are declared teaching contracts, not claims about a particular venue or employer.

summary: Tests need a contract, independent expectations and meaningful failure cases. Check properties only under their assumptions; finite passing cases are evidence, not universal proof.
